Source: UNMASKED-players-handbook.md § PART FOUR — THE BENEFIT POOL, with each pick's own printed text cited in place.

Two picks at character creation. Never again, never at level-up, never bought later. The pool is ten items, one pick each, and you have two slots to spend.

+10 HP · +10 MP · +5 HP and +5 MP · +4 IP · begin Projects · perform Rituals · See You Later · Unexpected Ally · Personal Vehicle · the Diabolist familiar — the familiar being the one pick that costs both slots.

How the two slots work

  • The familiar simply costs two slots. It is the pick that takes both, not a trade against the

other nine.

  • No pick repeats within the party except HP, MP and IP. The four stat picks may be taken by any

number of characters. Rituals do not contend either — Rituals grants Ritualism plus one named discipline, and any number of you may name the same one. Everything else is one character in the party, full stop.

  • Any Skill available in the pool cannot be chosen at level-up by anyone. Extra HP, Extra MP,

Extra IP, See You Later, Unexpected Ally and Personal Vehicle leave the level-up lists entirely; the pool is the only way into them.

  • Faithful Companion cannot be taken, at creation or at level-up. The familiar is the only

companion in the game, and one per party.

+10 HP

Source: Core Rulebook, Heroic Skills, p. 235 — EXTRA HP.

Permanently increase your maximum Hit Points by 10.

+10 MP

Source: Core Rulebook, Heroic Skills, p. 235 — EXTRA MP.

Permanently increase your maximum Mind Points by 10.

+5 HP and +5 MP

Source: UNMASKED-players-handbook.md § PART FOUR — the pool list. No printed Skill corresponds to this pick.

Permanently increase your maximum Hit Points by 5 and your maximum Mind Points by 5.

+4 IP

Source: Core Rulebook, Heroic Skills, p. 235 — EXTRA IP.

Permanently increase your maximum Inventory Points by 4.

Begin Projects

Source: Core Rulebook, printed p. 134, "Projects"; house rules from UNMASKED-players-handbook.md § PART FOUR and DRAFTS-ritual-project-guide-edits.md (ruled 6–7 Sep 2026).

You may initiate Projects — custom inventions built over days of work: explosive concoctions, magical devices, self-propelled magitech shields, even airships. You describe the invention's effects and how it operates; the GM sets its cost in materials from the area, potency and uses tables, and names a special ingredient for anything of medium potency or higher. You may negotiate a terrible flaw to cut the cost by 25%. Completion needs 1 progress for every 100 zenit of material cost, and a Project gains +1 progress per day for each character who worked on it.

The pool is the only door into Projects. No class skill grants them and no Keystone grants them — Inventor Prodigy and Traveling Workshop are Projects gates, and both still require this pick.

Projects serve the whole group: only one slow Project per rest, regardless of how many characters hold the pick.

Perform Rituals

Source: Core Rulebook, printed pp. 118–121; RITUALS-rosalinds-guide-adopted.md §1 (ruled 8 Sep 2026).

You gain Ritualism plus one other named discipline, and may perform Rituals of both.

Any number of you may name the same discipline. Discipline locking was removed entirely on 8 September 2026 — no school is contested, and no school is closed to the table.

The pool is one door into Rituals, not the only one. A class skill that explicitly grants Ritualism does grant it — investing the skill level is the gate, and no benefit pick is committed. A Keystone that grants a scoped Ritualism is a third door, and refunds nothing from the pool.

See You Later

Source: Core Rulebook, Rogue Skills, p. 201.

You may use an action and spend 1 Fabula Point to vanish from the current scene, reappearing whenever you want during a different scene in which another Player Character is present. Describe how you escaped and miraculously got there!

Unexpected Ally

Source: Core Rulebook, Orator Skills, p. 199.

You may use an action and spend 1 Fabula Point to choose a non-hostile creature able to hear and understand you. If you do, that creature becomes helpful towards you so long as you are kind and respectful to them and your requests are reasonable.

(The Heroic Skill Inspiring Presence interacts with this Skill.)

Personal Vehicle

Source: Techno Fantasy Atlas, Pilot Skills, pp. 159–169. The full frame, module and driving rules are on the compendium's Personal Vehicle page.

You gain a personal vehicle with a frame of your choice — Steed, Exoskeleton or Mecha. The frame is fixed for the rest of the game. Entering it during a conflict is an Objective action; leaving it costs no action but happens only on your turn. Only you may drive it, and passengers cannot Guard from inside. The maximum number of modules enabled at once is (3 + your Skill Level in Personal Vehicle).

ruled 8 Sep 2026. The pick counts as Skill Level = your level ÷ 10, minimum 1 — so the module cap is 3 + that, and it rises as you do. The vehicle comes with no free modules. The printed Skill hands you three when you acquire it; this pick does not. You find them, buy them, or earn them.

The Diabolist familiar (costs both picks)

Source: UNMASKED-players-handbook.md § PART FOUR. This is the whole of the written text.

A demon-shaped Aether construct. It may harvest a Skill from any fallen creature, and visibly, permanently takes on a trait of everything it consumes.

One per party. Taking it spends both of your benefit picks, and Faithful Companion is barred — the familiar is the only companion in the game.

ruled 8 Sep 2026 — the familiar's rules are the Techno Fantasy Atlas Diabolist quirk.

Source: Techno Fantasy Atlas — Quirk: Diabolist, p. 122.

Together with your group, create your familiar: a level 5 NPC belonging to the demon Species (Core Rulebook, page 302). This creature has no initiative score and does not level up, can have a maximum of two basic attacks, gains a +3 bonus to Accuracy Checks and Magic Checks, and their maximum Hit Points are equal to (five times the familiar's base Might die size + half your level).

When you reach level 20, your familiar gains an additional Skill. At level 40, your familiar gains another additional Skill. Make sure to discuss these Skill choices together with the rest of your group.

When an NPC you can see that belongs to the demon Species falls to 0 Hit Points, if you are present on the scene, you may spend 20 Mind Points. If you do, the Game Master reveals that creature's entire profile, and you may replace one of your familiar's Skills with one of that creature's Skills (the Game Master has final say on which Skills are eligible and how they apply to your familiar). Describe the transformation!

If you have this Quirk, you may not acquire the Faithful Companion Skill from the Wayfarer Class (Core Rulebook, page 217), and likewise you cannot gain this Quirk if you already acquired Faithful Companion.

Your familiar does not get an independent turn during conflicts, but you can use an action to have them perform an action (once per turn). If your familiar is affected by any turn-related effects (Core Rulebook, page 77), these are based on your turn. Your familiar joins and leaves scenes when you do, and gains your same benefits for rests. If reduced to 0 Hit Points, your familiar vanishes from the scene and reforms at your side at the start of the next scene in which you are present, with current HP equal to their Crisis score.
